why: All three checks pass; the finding survives. (1) DOC VERBATIM: curl -sL https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents.md (1250 lines) has the quoted sentence at :520 as a whole single-sentence bullet — '* The subagent's system prompt includes instructions for reading and writing to the memory directory.' No second clause reverses it. Its two sibling bullets at :521 and :522 carry the rest of the claimed behaviour verbatim ('the first 200 lines or 25KB of `MEMORY.md` ... whichever comes first'; 'Read, Write, and Edit tools are automatically enabled'), and :512-514 give the three directories. The one gating clause, :516 ('if you turn auto memory off ... the `memory` field has no effect'), does NOT excuse us: this fork HAS a live auto-memory subsystem (packages/shared/src/agent/memory/memory-store.ts, memory-cleanup.ts 'dream' pass, the `remember` tool, MEMORY.md records at global/workspace/project/session scope in capabilities/native-sources.ts), and there is no autoMemoryEnabled-equivalent master switch to be off — `grep -rna 'autoMemory'` finds only the marker/cleanup constants, no gate. (2) CITED FILE: packages/shared/src/agents/definitions.ts:90-95 reads exactly as claimed — the comment is 'Persistent memory scope for this agent (`user` / `project` / `local`). / Parsed, validated and carried; the per-agent memory DIRECTORY is not yet / provisioned — see the R30c report.' The scope type and its Claude-doc directory mapping are at :37-44, the strict normalizer at :366-370, and the throw-on-typo at :414/:427-428 ('Invalid <label>.memory: expected user, project or local'). The second cited site is exact: packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/runtime-agent-definitions.ts:173 is '...(descriptor.memory ? { memory: descriptor.memory } : {}),' — a pure spread pass-through. A third carrier the finding did not name: packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/runtime-agent-definition.ts:141 (descriptor field), :336-339 (runtime parse) and :616-620 (frontmatter parse), all validate-and-carry only. (3) CONSEQUENCE VERIFIED SEPARATELY FROM THE IDENTIFIER, both directions. Down: `grep -c -a memory packages/pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/spawner.ts` returns 0 — the module that actually spawns a subagent never sees the field, so nothing composes a memory prompt block from it and nothing force-enables Read/Write/Edit. Up: `grep -rna 'agent-memory' --include=*.ts --include=*.js --include=*.cjs --include=*.mjs packages apps` (with -a, per the NUL-byte trap) returns exactly two hits, both the doc comment at definitions.ts:40-41 — no directory is ever built or created. Sibling-subsystem check (the `disallowed-tools` shape): the fork's memory code IS a different subsystem — session/user/project MEMORY.md via native-sources.ts:910/1028/1093 and the capability `memory` view — and it is keyed on scope discovery, never on AgentDefinition.memory; naming it would be naming the wrong subsystem. Upstream-already-handled check: the Claude SDK backend cannot be quietly doing it either — claude-agent.ts has no `agents:` SDK option and no memory handling (its four `memory` hits are 'in-memory'/'memory growth' comments), and subagents run the Pi harness path. NOT one of the nine dated owner decisions in 2026-07-29-inert-worklist.md §3 (SEATBELT_TESTING_WILDCARD, availableModels/enforceAvailableModels, autoMode.classifyAllShell, ManagedDeliveryStateV1.drops, plugins/hooks-runtime.ts, SdkMcpServerConfig.required, SessionMirrorStore.delete, MirrorSessionKey.subpath/listSubkeys, listSessionSummaries) — it appears only as row 23 of the RAW sweep 2026-07-29-inert-contracts.md:95, the file that worklist's own header says is 'not the list to work from'. Not a deliberate product difference either: no subscription flow, no gateway scoping, no rename. What it IS is an already-recorded deviation that confirms rather than refutes: docs/superpowers/plans/2026-07-29-subagent-frontmatter.md:143 categorises `memory` as 'documented, not implemented — ... the per-agent memory DIRECTORY (agent-memory/<name>/, MEMORY.md injection, auto Read/Write/Edit) is a subsystem we do not have' (commit b31d6421), harvested into the deviation register at :306, and the parity audit's R30c row (2026-07-25 audit:698) says the same: 'costed with categories and NOT half-built'. Costed-and-deferred is an open gap, not a decision to keep it.
correctedState: Confirmed as a real divergence, with one clause of the submitted wording tightened. Accurate: `memory` is parsed and strictly validated against user|project|local in three places (definitions.ts:366-370 with a throw at :427-428; pi-harness/runtime-agent-definition.ts:336-339 and :616-620), carried on AgentDefinition (definitions.ts:95) and on the runtime descriptor (runtime-agent-definition.ts:141), and passed through to the orchestrator at pi-agent-server/src/orchestrator/runtime-agent-definitions.ts:173 — where consumption ends. spawner.ts contains zero occurrences of `memory`; no agent-memory/<name>/ directory is created anywhere (the string exists only in definitions.ts:40-41's doc comment); no MEMORY.md is injected on account of the field; no Read/Write/Edit force-enable exists. Overstated in the submission and corrected here: 'no memory prompt block is composed for a child' should read 'no PER-AGENT memory block is composed'. A child session does receive inherited MEMORY.md content as pinned `memory` context — the capability view's memory records survive child intersection (pi-harness/child-session-port.ts:188) and are added as pinned context at pi-harness/context-resource.ts:66 — but those come from the session/user/project MEMORY.md discovery in capabilities/native-sources.ts, are identical for every subagent, and are not keyed on the `memory:` field. Likewise 'cannot write the memory it is told it has' is only true when the AGENT AUTHOR writes memory instructions into the definition body (the doc's own tip at sub-agents.md:529-532); the host itself never tells the agent it has memory, which makes the field silently inert rather than actively misleading. Net: an author who writes `memory: project` gets strict validation, a definition that round-trips the value, and no cross-session learning of any kind.
